note: A chart labels an open region of a smooth manifold; the manifold supplies the points and compatible local structure.
Smooth transition maps between charts are part of the manifold atlas structure.
The transition is the composition of one chart with the inverse of another on their overlap.
A worldline can be understood as a curve passing through ordered spacetime events.
A worldline assigns each parameter value to a point of the spacetime manifold.
Worldline tangents are examples of tangent vectors at events.
The cotangent space is constructed as the vector-space dual of the tangent space at the same point.
Vector factors and vector inputs of a tensor belong to the tangent space at the field point.
Covector factors and the natural vector/covector pairing supply the dual slots used to construct multilinear tensors.
Tensor-field components change under coordinate transformations while the underlying geometric object remains the same.
Upper and lower index slots record the type of a tensor, while contraction pairs its vector-like and covector-like slots.
Differentiating the coordinate transition supplies the forward and inverse Jacobians used in each tensor index slot.
The component rule uses upper/lower slots and distinguishes summed old indices from free new indices.
Multilinearity of a tensor in its vector/covector inputs produces one basis-change factor for each index.
The invertible transition Jacobian makes equivalence of curve tangents and their vector-space operations independent of the chart.
Local charts turn a worldline into coordinate functions, allowing its smoothness and changes of description to be understood.
